title: Prove original Jensen inequality for constant-determinant fields when k>=1
statement: Let F=A+Dphi be any compatible periodic vector gradient with detF=d constant a.e.; determinant null-Lagrangian givesd=detA. For fixed d,write J=ell R_k(u,v,d)+d²,R=(ku-v+2d)²/[8(k+1)]+uv/4. Its(u,v)Hessian is [[k²,1],[1,1]]/[4(k+1)],positive semidefinite for k>=1. Derivatives R_u=(k²u+v+2kd)/[4(k+1)],R_v=(u+v-2d)/[4(k+1)] are nonnegative on u,v>=0,uv>=d²,by AM-GM with sign ofd retained. Since integral u>=u(A),integral v>=v(A),convexity then coordinate monotonicity give integralJ(F)>=J(A). This is a FULL positive theorem for arbitrary amplitudes,vector gradients and means under constant determinant andk>=1; it does not cover determinant fluctuations or1/3<k<1.
